1.1.title: Lesson 1.1: Exploring the Studica Robotics Kit
objectives: Identify structural aluminum extrusion channels and standard metric 8mm pitch patterns.
Distinguish between M3 and M4 screws (8mm, 12mm, 16mm) and understand Nyloc locknut mechanics.
Enforce mandatory lab safety rules (ANSI Z87.1 glasses, battery disconnect, loose clothing).
materials: Studica Robotics Kit storage bin per 2-student team
Divided plastic hardware sorting tray
2.5mm and 2.0mm ball-end hex keys
7.0mm open-end box wrench / nut driver
300mm stainless steel metric ruler
Safety glasses for all students

timeline.title: Safety Briefing & PPE Check
timeline.activity: Ensure every student is wearing safety glasses. Explain the rule of zero power during assembly.

timeline.title: Hardware Overview & Mechanics
timeline.activity: Demonstrate the 6061-T6 aluminum U-channel profile and explain the 8mm modular hole pitch.

timeline.title: Hands-On Sorting & Sizing
timeline.activity: Students sort screws into M3, M4x8, M4x12, M4x16 bins. Measure channels with metric rulers.

timeline.title: Joint Assembly Exercise
timeline.activity: Assemble sample 90° corner joint with two M4x12 bolts and Nyloc nuts. Guide proper torque technique.

timeline.title: Junior Rigidity Squeeze Challenge
timeline.activity: Teams perform the diagonal torsional squeeze test on their sample frames. Verify zero play.

timeline.title: Summary & Exit Ticket Review
timeline.activity: Conduct Exit Ticket check. Ensure all tools are accounted for and returned to bins.

misconceptions.pitfall: Students use standard nuts instead of Nylocs
misconceptions.intervention: Point out the blue nylon ring. Have students try to spin a Nyloc by hand vs a standard nut.

misconceptions.pitfall: Over-tightening and stripping hex socket heads
misconceptions.intervention: Demonstrate two-finger torque on the short arm of the hex key. Never use pliers on hex keys.
Teach the 'back-turn' rule: turn counter-clockwise until you feel a tiny click, then thread in.

differentiation.support: Provide a pre-printed 1:1 scale fastener identification sheet where students place screws directly on matching drawings.
differentiation.extension: Fast-finishing students assemble a 3D corner cube using 3 gusset plates and calculate total fastener mass using digital lab scale.

1.2.title: Lesson 1.2: Understanding the Robot Controller
objectives: Explain the architectural division of labor between Raspberry Pi 4 (brain), VMX-pi (reflexes), and Titan Quad (muscle).
Identify the key VMX-pi port groups: HiCurrDIO, FlexDIO, PWM, Analog, and CAN.
Wire and terminate a 1 Mbps differential CAN bus network with a 120-ohm terminating resistor.
materials: Assembled VMX-pi / Raspberry Pi 4 controller stack
Titan Quad DC Motor Controller (CAN ID 42)
Yellow/Green twisted pair CAN bus harness
2.5mm flathead terminal screwdriver
Digital multimeter set to DC Volts

timeline.title: Review & Objective
timeline.activity: Review fastener rules from Lesson 1.1. Introduce the concept of dual-brain architecture.

timeline.title: Dual-Brain Theory & CAN Bus
timeline.activity: Explain why Linux requires an FPGA coprocessor for microsecond timing. Explain differential CAN noise immunity.

timeline.title: Header Inspection & Port Mapping
timeline.activity: Students locate HiCurrDIO pins 20/21, FlexDIO pins 8-11, and the CAN port on their VMX-pi.

timeline.title: CAN Bus & Power Rail Wiring
timeline.activity: Connect twisted CAN pair to Titan CAN IN Weidmuller terminals. Set 120Ω termination switch to ON.

timeline.title: Zero Wire Snags Team Challenge
timeline.activity: Route cables cleanly inside extrusion cavity with spiral wrap and zip ties. Verify strain relief.

timeline.title: Exit Ticket & Terminal Verify
timeline.activity: Students answer Exit Ticket questions and execute candump command to observe Titan ID 42.

misconceptions.pitfall: Students plug 12V motor leads into 5V logic headers
misconceptions.intervention: Use color-coded tape to physically block off VMX headers until high-voltage power is completed.
Explain transmission line reflections (echo effect) using a skipping rope demonstration.
Mnemonic rule: Yellow = Sunshine (High), Green = Grass (Low).

differentiation.support: Provide students with a color-coded wiring diagram sticker to attach directly to their acrylic deck.
differentiation.extension: Have students run 'candump can0' in Linux terminal and decode the hexadecimal byte containing battery voltage.

1.3.title: Lesson 1.3: Building the Robot Chassis
objectives: Assemble the 240mm x 180mm x 100mm structural aluminum chassis.
Apply diagonal measurement techniques to eliminate chassis parallelogram distortion within ±0.5 mm.
Mount standoff hardware and fasten the laser-cut acrylic electronics deck securely.
materials: 2 x 240mm aluminum side extrusion channels
2 x 180mm aluminum cross extrusion channels
4 x 90-degree corner gusset plates
16 x M4x12mm socket-head bolts & 16 x M4 Nyloc nuts
4 x M3x20mm nylon standoffs & M3 button screws
Laser-cut acrylic electronics mounting deck
Precision digital caliper / 300mm steel metric ruler

timeline.title: Chassis Blueprint Walkthrough
timeline.activity: Show engineering drawing of 24x18cm footprint. Emphasize why squareness matters for straight driving.

timeline.title: Squaring Principles & Geometry
timeline.activity: Derive Pythagorean diagonal ($D = \sqrt{240^2 + 180^2} = 300\,\text{mm}$). Explain parallelogram drift.

timeline.title: Base Frame Assembly
timeline.activity: Students bolt channels and gussets together finger-tight. Measure diagonals $D_1$ and $D_2$.

timeline.title: Final Torquing & Acrylic Deck
timeline.activity: Torque all 8 corner bolts in X-pattern. Mount nylon standoffs and fasten acrylic baseplate.

timeline.title: The Caliper Audit Challenge
timeline.activity: Teacher inspects each chassis: verify $300\,\text{mm} \pm 0.5\,\text{mm}$ and zero table rocking.

timeline.title: Exit Ticket & Workspace Cleanup
timeline.activity: Review chassis dimension checklist and sign off student lab workbooks.

misconceptions.pitfall: Tightening bolts fully before measuring diagonals
misconceptions.intervention: Instruct students to leave nuts finger-loose until ruler confirms exact equal diagonals.
Enforce strict 'finger-tight only' rule on nylon standoffs to prevent stripped threads.

misconceptions.pitfall: Mounting channels with open U-profile facing outward
misconceptions.intervention: Ensure U-channels face INWARD so wires and batteries can sit safely inside the frame cavity.

differentiation.support: Provide pre-cut wooden 300mm diagonal alignment jigs that drop directly into the frame corners.
differentiation.extension: Have students calculate the moment of inertia and torsional stiffness of the chassis frame.

1.4.title: Lesson 1.4: Installing Motors and Wheels
objectives: Mount 60:1 Maverick planetary gearmotors using aluminum clamping brackets.
Derive and explain the 1,680 ticks/rev quadrature encoder formula ($28 \times 60 = 1680$).
Install 100mm rubber drive wheels with blue threadlocker on D-shaft set screws and align rear omni caster.
materials: 2 x Studica Maverick 12V DC Planetary Gearmotors (60:1)
2 x Aluminum clamping motor mounts & M4 clamping hardware
2 x 6mm steel D-shaft hex wheel couplers & set screws
2 x 100mm high-traction rubber drive wheels & M3 mounting screws
1 x Smooth omnidirectional ball caster wheel & standoff spacers
1 x Bottle Blue Threadlocker (Loctite 242)
Wooden test blocks (to elevate robot wheels during bench testing)

timeline.title: Drivetrain Overview
timeline.activity: Introduce planetary gear reduction and encoder feedback. Emphasize rotating machinery safety.

timeline.title: Gear Ratio & Kinematics Math
timeline.activity: Derive 1680 ticks/rev ($28 \times 60$). Calculate 100mm wheel circumference ($C = 314.16\,\text{mm}$) and 0.187 mm/tick.

timeline.title: Motor & Wheel Installation
timeline.activity: Mount gearmotors into clamping brackets. Fasten hex hubs onto D-shaft flat face with threadlocker.

timeline.title: Rear Caster Alignment & Harness
timeline.activity: Install rear omni caster. Plug motor harnesses into Titan Channels M0 (Left) and M1 (Right).

timeline.title: Roll-Out Resistance Challenge
timeline.activity: Perform 5-degree ramp roll-out test. Listen for quiet, smooth mechanical hum from planetary gearboxes.

timeline.title: Exit Ticket & Bench Audit
timeline.activity: Complete Worksheet 04 calculation table and review encoder derivation.

misconceptions.pitfall: Tightening the set screw against the rounded side of the D-shaft
misconceptions.intervention: Shine a flashlight into the hub bore to visually confirm the set screw is aligned with the flat face.

misconceptions.pitfall: Forgetting threadlocker on motor set screws
misconceptions.intervention: Demonstrate how motor vibration shakes unglued set screws loose within 5 minutes of driving.

misconceptions.pitfall: Omitting the 1mm clearance gap between wheel and frame
misconceptions.intervention: Use a 1mm guitar pick or business card as a spacer between the hex coupler and the bearing face.

differentiation.support: Pre-mark the flat face of motor D-shafts with a bright paint marker for easy visual alignment.
differentiation.extension: Have students write a 5-line Python script that reads live encoder ticks as the wheel is turned by hand.

1.5.title: Lesson 1.5: Power and Wiring Hygiene
objectives: Construct a segregated 12V DC power distribution tree with a 20A automotive blade fuse.
Execute a mandatory digital multimeter polarity audit to prevent catastrophic reverse polarity.
Apply professional wire routing hygiene: separate high-current motor cables from low-voltage signals.
materials: 12V 3000mAh NiMH battery pack with yellow XT60 connector
Inline rubber fuse holder & 20-Amp yellow automotive blade fuse
Heavy-duty SPST toggle switch & rear chassis mounting bracket
14 AWG high-flex silicone wire (Red positive, Black ground)
Digital multimeter with needle probes
Wire strippers & small flathead terminal screwdriver
Spiral cable wrap & miniature zip ties

timeline.title: Electrical Safety Protocol
timeline.activity: Enforce zero battery connection until multimeter audit is signed off by teacher. Explain reverse polarity.

timeline.title: Power Topology & Fuse Protection
timeline.activity: Explain segregated power tree (muscle vs brain). Show how a 20A fuse prevents battery fires and short circuits.

timeline.title: Power Wiring & Switch Installation
timeline.activity: Install fuse, mount toggle switch, strip 14 AWG wire, and clamp firmly into Titan VIN (+) and GND (-) terminals.

timeline.title: Multimeter Polarity Audit
timeline.activity: Teacher observes each team probe switch output with multimeter. Confirm positive +12V DC reading.

timeline.title: The 5G Tug & Shake Challenge
timeline.activity: Gently tug wires and shake robot: zero rattling, zero loose terminals. Flip switch: solid green LEDs!

timeline.title: Module 1 Wrap-Up & Graduation
timeline.activity: Celebrate the completion of the physical robot build! Issue Module 1 completion stamp.

misconceptions.pitfall: Clamping screw terminal onto wire insulation jacket
misconceptions.intervention: Inspect the terminal window with a magnifying glass or flashlight: copper must be visible under screw head.

misconceptions.pitfall: Relying on wire color without multimeter verification
misconceptions.intervention: Always test with a multimeter! Assume nothing in electrical engineering.

misconceptions.pitfall: Leaving battery loose inside the chassis
misconceptions.intervention: Demonstrate what happens in a sudden robot stop: an unstrapped battery slides forward and tears wires.

differentiation.support: Provide pre-stripped and tinned wire leads with ferrules to make screw terminal insertion foolproof.
differentiation.extension: Have students measure quiescent idle current draw of the robot using an in-line DC clamp ammeter.

T0.title: Lesson T0: Teacher Robot Commissioning & Lab Setup
objectives: Automate the flashing, networking, and provisioning of the Studica VMX-pi Ubuntu 22.04 environment.
Deploy CycloneDDS routing XML configuration bound to static Ethernet IP 172.22.11.2.
Configure the unified systemd background service (robot.service) to prevent pigpio memory collisions.
materials: Teacher laptop running Ubuntu 22.04 with ROS 2 Humble
Cat6 RJ45 Gigabit Ethernet cable
Studica VMX-pi Controller with freshly flashed micro-SD card
Commissioning script: teacher_commission_robot.sh

timeline.title: Ethernet Link & SSH Key Exchange
timeline.activity: Connect laptop to robot via Ethernet. Configure laptop IP 172.22.11.247 and verify passwordless SSH.

timeline.title: Executing Commissioning Script
timeline.activity: Run ./teacher_commission_robot.sh: deploys CycloneDDS XML, CAN ID 42 configs, and udev rules.

timeline.title: Service Validation & Hardware Daemon
timeline.activity: Check systemctl status robot.service. Confirm pigpio single-daemon lock.

timeline.title: Lab Fleet Mass Provisioning
timeline.activity: Repeat procedure across all team robots. Tag each robot with assigned team number.

misconceptions.pitfall: Allowing students to run apt-get or build ROS 2 packages during class
misconceptions.intervention: Strictly pre-install all offline Debian packages and ROS 2 libraries before day 1.

misconceptions.pitfall: Multiple processes attempting to access VMX pigpio hardware simultaneously
misconceptions.intervention: Ensure manual_composition handles all digital I/O, motors, and encoders in one service.

differentiation.support: Keep a clone image of a fully configured micro-SD card ready for instant swapping in case of SD corruption.
differentiation.extension: Set up a local DHCP and TFTP server to PXE-boot or network-clone student laptops.

T1.title: Lesson T1: Pre-Flight Hardware Health Check
objectives: Run automated Python hardware diagnostic script (verify_robot_health.py).
Verify CAN bus communication with Titan Quad Controller (CAN ID 42) and battery telemetry.
Verify navX 9-axis IMU gyro calibration and YDLidar laser rotation.
materials: Commissioned Studica AMR robot on wooden bench support blocks
Fully charged 12V 3000mAh NiMH battery
Student laptop with test scripts in Documents/studica_amr_course/scripts

timeline.title: Power & Voltage Check
timeline.activity: Power ON robot. Check battery voltage: must be >12.4V. Verify green/blue LEDs.

timeline.title: Automated Sensor Suite Audit
timeline.activity: Run python3 verify_robot_health.py: tests motors M0/M1, encoders, IMU, and LiDAR.

timeline.title: Fleet Sign-Off & Lab Readiness
timeline.activity: Confirm all test output shows [✓] PASS. Elevate wheels and place ready for students.

misconceptions.pitfall: Running motor tests while robot wheels are resting on the table
misconceptions.intervention: Always elevate the robot frame on a wooden block so moving wheels do not launch the robot off the desk!

differentiation.support: Create a 1-page laminated pre-flight checklist attached to each robot workstation.
differentiation.extension: Integrate automated Slack or email alerts when any robot battery drops below 11.5V.
